absent: Numeric ABI values for signal numbers, error codes, mask operation selectors, pidfd flags and layout tags are not shown in these fragments.
Full definitions of task, signal hand, sigaction, pending queue and siginfo structures beyond the fields touched here.
Internals of freezing, tracing, stopping, orphan group detection, coredump, permission checks and generic kill routing helpers.
Post copy validation rules for native and compat signal information and the complete layout decoding table.
Scheduler sleep, high resolution timeout and freezer interaction details beyond the observed wait and restore behaviour.
Compat mask and time conversion helpers and pid namespace and pid file lifecycle beyond the observed checks.

findings.text: The restart system entry invokes the per task restart callback stored for the current thread and returns its result. A separate no restart helper exists that always reports interruption so callers that have nothing to restart fail with an interrupted status.

The internal mask routine optionally reports the prior blocked set, then derives a successor by adding the input set for block, removing it for unblock, or replacing for set, and rejects unknown operation selectors. It assumes only the current thread mutates its own blocked set and therefore needs no locking.

Native and compat mask changing entries validate that the caller size matches the kernel mask size, snapshot the prior mask for output, fetch the proposed set, remove the two unblockable signals from it, delegate to the internal updater, and copy the prior mask back to user memory with fault reported on copy failure.

Temporary mask installers treat a null user pointer as successful no operation, otherwise require an exact size and a successful fetch from user space, then arm deferred restore, preserve the current mask as the saved mask, and install the fetched mask as the new blocked set.

Pending reporting merges thread private and process shared pending sets under the signal hand lock, then outside the lock intersects that union with the current blocked set, so the result contains only pending signals that are currently blocked.

Native and compat pending query entries reject oversized caller buffers, collect the blocked pending set through a shared helper, and transfer the result to user space using the native or compat copy path respectively.

A small read only table maps several signals to a pair of limit and layout attributes. Fault related signals share a fault layout with per signal code limits, while child, poll and system signals each map to their own dedicated layout kind, with an optional extra fault entry when the corresponding signal exists.

Inbound signal information is copied from user memory with fault reported on failure, the signal number field is forced to the caller supplied number, and post copy validation is applied. A dispatcher selects the native or 32 bit compat copy path based on whether the caller is in a compat system call.

Outbound translation to the 32 bit form clears the destination, copies the common number error and code fields, then copies only the fields relevant to the decoded layout kind, narrowing address and related pointer fields for the smaller address size. The user copy wrapper reports a fault if the destination cannot be written.

Timed waiting first validates the optional timeout and builds a wait mask that can never include the two unblockable signals. It attempts an immediate dequeue under lock, and when empty with a nonzero timeout it temporarily narrows the current blocked set to the waited subset while preserving the original, sleeps in an interruptible freezable state with a bounded high resolution timeout, then restores the original mask and retries the dequeue. A dequeued number is returned, otherwise interruption and timeout are distinguished.

Four timed wait entries cover native and compat mask representations crossed with native and 32 bit timeout representations. Each validates the mask size, fetches the wait set and optional timeout from user space, delegates to a common waiter, and copies signal information out only when a signal was actually dequeued.

Kill style signal information is built by clearing the record, setting the signal number, zeroing the error field, choosing a thread versus user origin code based on scope, and stamping the sender thread group identity and user identity. Separately, a predicate treats nonnegative codes and the thread kill code as reserved for kernel use.
The classic kill entry forwards its signal number and target identifier to a generic send helper using a no extra information mode, leaving target interpretation and permission checks to that helper.

Pid file descriptor handling checks that the target pid namespace is the active namespace or an ancestor of it by walking parent links, failing when the chain ends without a match. Resolution prefers the thread scoped translation and falls back to the thread group scoped translation when the first reports absence.

The set of valid pidfd send scope flags consists of exactly three mutually exclusive selectors for thread, thread group and process group delivery. Callers must supply at most one of them with all other flag bits clear.

Pidfd sending validates that only known flag bits are set and that at most one scope selector is present, resolves self thread and self thread group shortcuts to the current task with reference counting, otherwise resolves the file to a pid with namespace access checked and a default scope inferred from the file mode. User supplied information must match the requested signal number and may carry kernel reserved codes only when signalling self in a narrow scope, otherwise a freshly built kill record is used, with process group scope routed to group delivery and other scopes routed to typed pid delivery.

Targeted delivery looks up the thread by virtual identifier under read side protection with an optional thread group match, checks permission, treats a zero signal as an existence and permission probe without queueing, otherwise queues a private signal and maps a narrow sighand race failure to success. Thread kill builds a thread scoped kill record before delegating to this path.
Thread and thread group kill entries reject nonpositive identifiers and delegate to a common thread kill helper that builds appropriate signal information and performs the targeted send.

Queued signal information paths copy the user record in native or compat form, reject kernel reserved codes arriving from a different sender, and route process wide requests to process delivery versus thread specific requests to targeted delivery after validating positive identifiers for the thread group variant.

A kernel internal installer updates the handler for a given signal under lock, and when installing ignore it additionally discards already queued instances of that signal from both shared and private queues and recomputes the pending state.

The delivery scan cycles through frozen handling, synchronous fault dequeue with fallback to general dequeue, optional tracer rewrite, delivery tracing, and disposition classification. Ignore, user handler with optional one shot reset, kernel ignored default, unkillable filtering, stop handling and fatal termination are distinct terminal or continuing outcomes, with stop and fatal paths releasing the lock and either reentering the scan or exiting the thread group.

Fault originated signals are dequeued ahead of other pending signals so architectural state points at the fault. Ignored handlers, kernel ignored defaults and unkillable discards cause continued scanning rather than delivery, while stop defaults attempt a group stop and all other defaults proceed to fatal handling with an optional core dump phase.

The signal hand irq saving lock is held across dequeue, disposition inspection, pending merging and handler installation. It is explicitly released around the orphaned process group test and before core dump and group exit work, with the scan re acquiring it before continuing, preserving ordering against the task list lock.

Timed waiting holds the signal hand lock only for dequeue and mask swap operations and releases it while sleeping. Targeted sending uses read side critical sections for task lookup without holding the signal lock across the whole operation. The current blocked mask is updated without locking because only the current thread touches it outside interrupt context.

Successful delivery clears the deferred restore flag, unions the handler mask into the blocked set and additionally blocks the delivered signal itself unless no deferral was requested, disarms the alternate stack when auto disarm is set, and optionally notifies the tracer when single stepping. The setup completion wrapper forces a fault signal when frame setup failed and otherwise performs the delivery update.

Releasing the signal lock for the orphan check and for fatal handling opens windows where new signals may arrive, requiring revalidation on relock and explaining why a stop attempt may be abandoned. Concurrent fatal arrivals can race on the shared group exit code with the loser adopting the winner value, and worker threads with mandatory cleanup must not be force exited on this path.

User controlled sizes, masks, timeouts and pointers are validated before use, with size mismatch, invalid timeout and copy faults reported as errors. Narrowing of the blocked set during sleep must be paired with restoration of the saved mask even when the sleep is interrupted, otherwise the thread would retain an unintended mask.

Two signals remain unblockable and unwaitable across mask install, mask query and timed wait operations and are always stripped from user supplied sets. The mask operation selector distinguishes block, unblock and set modes, with any other value rejected.

Per task restart and masking state includes a restart callback invoked by the restart entry, a current blocked set, a saved mask used with deferred restore, a real blocked stash used across timed waiting, and an alternate stack flag word supporting auto disarm. These fields are read and updated by the restart, mask and wait paths described here.

Mask manipulation and 32 bit signal information translation helpers are available for use beyond this file. They encapsulate blocked set updates, temporary user mask installation with restore bookkeeping, and layout aware narrowing of signal information for compat consumers.
